page.title: Settings
page.subtitle: Configure your UltraTorrent instance.
page.emptyDescription: This instance does not expose editable settings yet.
page.generalDescription: Values are validated by the server on save.

rootPath.title: Default Root Path
rootPath.description: Users can browse only inside this root path. Parent folders and system directories outside it are blocked.
rootPath.error: Could not load the root path.
rootPath.notWritableWarning: The app process cannot write to this path — downloads and folder creation there will fail.
rootPath.label: Root path

help.before: Must be a directory within the server's configured storage roots (
help.after: ). Browsing can only be narrowed within these, never widened past them.

bandwidth.title: Per-engine bandwidth
bandwidth.description: A ceiling applied to each torrent engine separately. The Activity Scheduler overrides it only on engines it is actually managing.
bandwidth.emptyMeansUnlimited: Leave a field empty for unlimited. Nothing is applied to any engine until you save a ceiling here.
bandwidth.unreachable: These engines cannot apply a global rate limit, so these values do not reach them: {{engines}}
bandwidth.saveFailed: Could not save the bandwidth limits
bandwidth.aggregate_one: This ceiling is in force on {{count}} engine, so it is also your installation total.
bandwidth.aggregate_other: This ceiling is in force on {{count}} engines, and each gets the full amount — so the most UltraTorrent can use altogether is {{down}} down and {{up}} up. Every shipped engine sets its own limit and cannot see the others, so there is no shared total to enforce.

publicUrl.title: Public URL
publicUrl.description: The address this instance is reachable at from outside your network. Links that leave the building — newsletters, unsubscribe pages, shared reports — are built from it.
publicUrl.hint: Scheme and host only, with a port if it is not the default. No path, no query, no credentials.
publicUrl.saveFailed: Could not save the public URL
publicUrl.checkFailed: Could not check the public URL
publicUrl.certNote: Certificates are reported here, not issued. This application runs in a container that does not hold ports 80 or 443, so obtaining and renewing a certificate belongs to whatever terminates TLS in front of it.

check.httpsPlaintext: links sent out will be plaintext
check.acmePort: Port 80 is open for certificate renewal
check.acmeClosed: closed — Let's Encrypt validates on port 80 and nowhere else

guide.unreachable: Nothing answered. Check that the hostname points at this network and that the port is forwarded to this host.
guide.httpCanIssue: Port 80 is reachable, so a Let's Encrypt certificate can be issued for this hostname. Set it up on whatever terminates TLS in front of this instance, then change this URL to https.
guide.httpNoPort80: Traffic to this address is unencrypted, and port 80 is closed so a certificate cannot be issued over HTTP-01. Forward port 80 to this host, or use a DNS-01 challenge instead.
guide.selfSignedCanIssue: This is a self-signed certificate, so every visitor sees a warning. Port 80 is reachable, so a real Let's Encrypt certificate can replace it.
guide.untrusted: Browsers will reject this certificate. Replace it with one from a public certificate authority.
guide.expiring: The certificate expires in {{days}} days. If renewal is automatic, confirm it still works — a port 80 forward removed after issuance breaks renewal silently.
guide.ok: This address is reachable and its certificate is trusted.
